description: Safety Shepherd capabilities manifest — per-agent grants. Decision = ALLOW | BLOCK | ESCALATE. Edit grants here; no code change needed.
_blocked_paths_comment: fnmatch('**/.env', '.env') is False — a '**/' prefix still requires a slash. Every pattern therefore needs a root-level twin, or a secret sitting at the top of the tree slips through for any agent whose file_paths grant reaches the root.

governor._comment: Phase 2 capability-token minter. Every plan-verify call arrives with category='docker' (shepherd_client.py hardcodes it) and tool=the requested action's literal kind string -- pydantic's Literal on RequestedAction.kind closes that set to exactly the strings on that Literal (3 as of Phase 2b: compose_profile.preview, crew.workflow.preview, container.restart -- 'tools' below is deliberately NOT updated to include the third; see BROski recover Phase 2b, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-broski-recover-2b-design.md §9.2, for why no grant was added). Grant the literal strings, not the coarse 'docker' capability other agents get: rule 7 (tool not in allowlist) checks the tool string first, so 'docker' alone would still ESCALATE at rule 9 on every real request. No file_paths/domains: governor never touches files or makes outbound calls other than this /evaluate round trip.

coder_studio._comment: HyperStudio write path. Targets arrive worktree-relative, so '**' means 'anywhere inside the throwaway worktree' — the boundary is enforced in coder-studio/shepherd.py before this manifest is consulted. blocked_paths still wins (rule 2 precedes rule 5). 'bash' is deliberately NOT granted: its target is a shell command, which the blocked_paths globs cannot read.

coder-agent._comment: The orchestrator sends the HYPHENATED name; policy._agent_caps is an exact-key lookup, so this agent used to fall through to the '*' wildcard and its per-agent entry (coder_agent) never applied. This entry is the wildcard's rights PLUS exactly one crew tool (least privilege, separation of duties). Added 2026-10-03; see docs/IDE_HEALTH_REPORT_2026-10-03.md.
